directive.name: typescript
directive.description: Type safety, domain modeling, and API design requirements for strict TypeScript

context.principle: Never use any - use unknown and narrow with type guards
All exported functions must have explicit return types
Use branded types for domain identifiers (TaskId, ProjectId, etc.)
Use discriminated unions for states, not boolean flags

process.rule: Define domain types for new identifiers using branded types
Use readonly on value objects and interface properties
Use options objects for functions with more than 2 parameters

check.reason: any type disables type checking - use unknown and narrow
as any is an escape hatch - fix the underlying type issue
ts-ignore suppresses errors - fix the type issue or link to issue

check.item: No any type in new code
All exported functions have explicit return types
Domain types used for IDs (not raw strings)
Discriminated unions for states (not boolean flags)

example.explanation: any disables type checking, making access unsafe
unknown requires proper type narrowing before use
Branded types prevent mixing up different ID types
Boolean flags allow impossible states (isLoading AND isComplete both true)
Only one state is possible at a time, enabling exhaustive handling
